what_is_open: The exact minimax exponent and a matching positive-band converse on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\), removal of the logarithmic factor on the remainder of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), and the frontier under the opposite nuisance-smoothness ordering remain unresolved.
obstruction: The frozen primitives provide only the oracle pointwise-regression lower branch.  The candidate density-coupled and asymmetric handles name perturbation programs but establish neither model membership, target separation, nor an \(n\)-sample testing-distance bound.  Consequently no declared result matches the close-pair upper exponent \(t\) or the broader rank-capped upper endpoint.
attempted: The available route combines the proved close-pair estimator with the oracle two-point bump lower bound and checks whether the resulting endpoints coincide.  They do not: \(t<q\).  The candidate density-perturbation and unequal-resolution programs cannot be invoked because their load-bearing testing properties are explicitly unproved.
partial_result:
On
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}
=\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\cap
\{(\alpha,\beta,\gamma):0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\},
\]
the established close-pair upper theorem and oracle lower theorem give,
uniformly over compact subsets,
\[
c n^{-q}\leq R_n^{\mathrm{band}}
\leq C n^{-t}=C r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}},
\qquad
t=\left(1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{4s}\right)^{-1},
\qquad
q=\frac{\gamma}{2\gamma+d},
\qquad t<q.
\]
Thus benchmark-rate achievability without density estimation or density
smoothness is proved on this nonempty region, and the logarithmic loss of the
broader rank-capped upper bound is absent there.  On the remainder of
\(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), the proved bracket is
\[
c n^{-q}\leq R_n^{\mathrm{band}}
\leq Cn^{-p}(\log n)^{2p},
\qquad
p=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{d}<q.
\]
Finally, the definition of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\) itself imposes
\(\beta<\alpha\); hence the opposite ordering \(\alpha<\beta\) lies outside
the presently defined low-smoothness region and has no frontier conclusion in
this core.
